title: How to register unmanaged databases, Snowflake and Databricks in DSPM, with credentials and the database roles the pages give

prose.text: {{unmanaged-prereqs}} The other registration types are in [[dspm.service-registration]]; see also [[dspm.overview]], [[dspm.scanning:authentication]] and [[dspm.scanning:database-sampling]].

prose.label: Engines and credentials.
prose.text: {{unmanaged-engines}} {{unmanaged-auth-types}} {{unmanaged-entra-sp}} {{unmanaged-secret-location}} The Azure location for an unmanaged database is stated two ways on the page {{divergence:azure-unmanaged-secret-location}}. {{unmanaged-hashicorp}}

prose.label: Snowflake edit page.
prose.text: The add and edit pages name the secret store ambiguously {{gap:snowflake-edit-secret-wording}}.

prose.label: Databricks gaps.
prose.text: Whether a GCP Databricks workspace is supported is open {{gap:databricks-gcp}}. The permission script contents are not shown {{gap:databricks-script-contents}}.

checks.do: Where the credential secret must be stored for the database type: unmanaged, on-premises or Snowflake; for an Azure unmanaged database the page gives two different locations, so see the divergence.
Whether the Databricks registration type is Account, which the page says is available only for AWS.

unmanaged-prereqs.statement: Adding unmanaged databases requires onboarding the account with a custom model, security groups allowing the scanner or orchestrator subnets, a custom role to configure SQL authentication, and SQL connection strings with credentials.

quotes: 1. Onboard the account using a custom model to establish network connectivity between DSPM and the unmanaged database.
2. Modify security groups to allow connections from the scanner or orchestrator subnets.
3. Create a custom role with required permissions to configure SQL authentication.
4. Provide SQL connection strings and authentication credentials to allow DSPM to access the unmanaged database.

unmanaged-engines.statement: Database engine choices for an unmanaged database are MS SQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, MySQL or MongoDB; for Oracle the connection string type is selectable.

quotes: Database Engine: Select the database engine type (MS SQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, MySQL, or MongoDB).
4. Type of Connection String (for Oracle Only): Select any of the following connection strings:

unmanaged-auth-types.statement: Authentication Type options for Azure Key Vault or AWS Secrets Manager providers are SQL Authentication, Microsoft Entra Service Principal, Microsoft Entra Authentication with user-managed identity, SCRAM Authentication or X.509 Authentication; SCRAM and X.509 are for the MongoDB engine only.

quotes: Authentication Type: Select the authentication type (SQL Authentication, Microsoft Entra Service Principal, Microsoft Entra Authentication with user-managed identity, SCRAM Authentication, or X.509 Authentication).
SCRAM Authentication, or X.509 Authentication (for MongoDB database engine only)

unmanaged-secret-location.statement: The SQL authentication table on the Adding Unmanaged Databases page says where the password secret must be stored depends on the database type: unmanaged databases use the target AWS account or any Key Vault of the target subscription; on-premises databases use the orchestrator account, the worker plane resource group Key Vault in Azure, or the orchestrator GCP project.

quotes: SQL Authentication (For Azure, AWS, and On-Premises)
In order for DSPM to read the password and connect to the database, ensure you do the following:
| Unmanaged | AWS: Create and store the secret in the AWS target account. Azure: Create and store the secret in any Key Vault of the target subscription. |
| On-premises | AWS: Create and store the secret in the AWS account where the orchestrator account is present.
Azure: Create and store the secret in the Key Vault of the worker plane resource group [integration_id_worker_plane_rg] of the subscription where the orchestrator account is present.
GCP: Create and store the secret in the secret manager of the GCP project where the orchestrator account is present. |

unmanaged-entra-sp.statement: The Microsoft Entra Service Principal section is headed for Azure only, yet it also has an AWS Secret Manager ARN (for AWS) field; its Key Vault URI (for Azure) must be available in the same account as the unmanaged database, with the Key Vault expected to follow the Azure role-based access control permission model.

quotes: - Microsoft Entra Service Principal (for Azure only)
AWS Secret Manager ARN (for AWS): Enter the ARN of the AWS Secret Manager.
This URI must be available in the same account where the unmanaged database is present, and the Key Vault should follow the Azure role-based access control permission model.

unmanaged-hashicorp.statement: With a self-hosted HashiCorp Vault, network policies must allow inbound connectivity from the DSPM scanner subnets to the Vault and the databases, and a DSPM user must be created in the Vault.

quotes: Ensure the network policies allow inbound connectivity from the DSPM scanner subnets to the HashiCorp Vault and unmanaged databases.
Create a DSPM user in the HashiCorp Vault for authentication.

unmanaged-bulk-template.statement: Bulk registration uses a downloaded ZIP of two templates, cloud_unmanageddb.xlsx and onprem_unmanageddb.xlsx; the uploaded file name must be exactly one of these names to prevent errors.

quotes: - cloud_unmanageddb.xlsx for cloud databases
- onprem_unmanageddb.xlsx for on‑premises databases
The uploaded file name must be exactly onprem_unmanageddb.xlsx for on‑premises databases or cloud_unmanageddb.xlsx for cloud databases, to prevent errors.

unmanaged-onprem-scanner.statement: For an on-premises unmanaged database, the On-Premise Scanner section is populated automatically if the data center has on-premises scanners; otherwise a scanner must be integrated with the data center.

quotes: If the data center has on-premises scanners, then the On-Premise Scanner section is automatically populated with the available integrations. If not, integrate an on-premises scanner with the data center.

unmanaged-edit-timing.statement: Unmanaged database configuration changes take effect only at the next scheduled scan.

quotes: Changes made to the database server configuration take effect only at the next scheduled scan.

mssql-role.statement: For unmanaged MS SQL, a server role (ReadOnlyServerRole) is granted VIEW ANY DATABASE, CONNECT ANY DATABASE and VIEW ANY DEFINITION, and a login is created for SQL, managed identity or service principal authentication.

quotes: GRANT VIEW ANY DATABASE TO ReadOnlyServerRole; GRANT CONNECT ANY DATABASE TO ReadOnlyServerRole; GRANT VIEW ANY DEFINITION TO ReadOnlyServerRole;
CREATE LOGIN [service_principal_name] FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER;
CREATE LOGIN [user_managed_identity_name] FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER;
CREATE LOGIN dspmloginuser WITH PASSWORD

mssql-new-db-trigger.statement: A server-level trigger GrantReadAccessOnNewDatabase is created so that read access is assigned automatically to newly created MS SQL databases.

quotes: Creates a trigger to automatically assign permissions to new databases.
CREATE TRIGGER GrantReadAccessOnNewDatabase ON ALL SERVER FOR CREATE_DATABASE

postgres-role.statement: For unmanaged PostgreSQL, read-only access is given by granting SELECT on all tables in the public schema to the user.

quotes: GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO <USERNAME>;
the assigned role or user account has read-only access to all tables in the public schema

mongo-roles.statement: For unmanaged MongoDB, a user needs readAnyDatabase (read-only on all databases except local and config) and clusterMonitor (monitoring and cluster metadata), both assigned in the admin database.

quotes: readAnyDatabase: Grants the scanner read-only access to all databases, excluding the local and config databases.
clusterMonitor: Provides read-only access to monitoring and cluster-level metadata
These roles must be assigned within the admin database to ensure cross-database visibility.

oracle-user.statement: For unmanaged Oracle (on-premises, AWS EC2 or Azure VM), a common user C##READ_USER is created with CONTAINER=ALL and granted SELECT_CATALOG_ROLE and SELECT ANY TABLE, and CONTAINER_DATA=ALL is set; the default listener port is 1521.

quotes: The C## prefix and CONTAINER=ALL clause are required for common users in an Oracle Container Database (CDB).
GRANT SELECT_CATALOG_ROLE TO C##READ_USER CONTAINER=ALL; GRANT SELECT ANY TABLE TO C##READ_USER CONTAINER=ALL;
ALTER USER C##READ_USER SET CONTAINER_DATA=ALL CONTAINER=CURRENT;
The default port is 1521, though your Oracle instance might be configured to use a different, custom port.

snowflake-warehouse-role.statement: Snowflake registration needs a dedicated warehouse (created x-small by default) and a role granted MONITOR SECURITY and MONITOR USAGE on the account and the SNOWFLAKE.SECURITY_VIEWER database role.

quotes: A dedicated warehouse is required so that DSPM has the necessary resources in Snowflake.
CREATE OR ALTER WAREHOUSE dspmwarehouse; - By default this will create with size x-small
grant MONITOR SECURITY ON ACCOUNT to role dspmdatascanrole; grant MONITOR USAGE ON ACCOUNT to role dspmdatascanrole; GRANT DATABASE ROLE SNOWFLAKE.SECURITY_VIEWER TO ROLE dspmdatascanrole;

snowflake-grant-procedure.statement: A z_dspm_grant_db_read procedure runs grants on non-shared Snowflake databases; an optional Snowflake task re-runs it (the example schedule is daily at 2am UTC) to cover newly added databases.

quotes: CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE z_dspm_grant_db_read()
RETURN grants || ' grants executed on non-shared databases.'
Optional: In case you want this DSPM role to automatically discover and scan the newly added databases, run the following command once.
schedule = 'USING CRON 0 2 * * * UTC' -- runs every day at 2am UTC; edit as needed

snowflake-user-auth.statement: The Snowflake DSPM user authenticates with either a programmatic access token (PAT) or an RSA key pair (generated as unencrypted or passphrase-encrypted).

quotes: Basic Authentication (Using PAT)
Generate a programmatic access token (PAT) for this newly created user from the Snowflake UI.
openssl genrsa 2048 | openssl pkcs8 -topk8 -inform PEM -out rsa_key.p8 -nocrypt
openssl genrsa 2048 | openssl pkcs8 -topk8 -v2 des3 -inform PEM -out rsa_key.p8

snowflake-network-policy.statement: A Snowflake network rule allowing ingress from the public IP of the NAT used for scanning is attached as a network policy to the DSPM user.

quotes: Network policy allows communication between the DSPM components deployed in the customer scanner account and Snowflake.
CREATE NETWORK RULE ALLOW_INGRESS_ZSCALER_POLICY MODE = 'INGRESS' TYPE = 'IPV4' VALUE_LIST = ('xx.xx.xx.xx');
Get the public IP address of the NAT that will be used to perform the data scan.
ALTER USER dspmdatascanuser SET NETWORK_POLICY = ALLOW_INGRESS_ZSCALER_POLICY;

snowflake-azure-cli.statement: When DSPM components are deployed in Azure, the private key secret is created with the Azure CLI because the Azure portal does not support multiple inputs for secrets.

quotes: When deploying DSPM components in Azure, a specific configuration is required to ensure secure communication with Snowflake.
Use the Azure CLI to create a private key and secret, as the Azure portal does not support multiple inputs for secrets.

snowflake-secret-location.statement: Snowflake credentials must be stored in the AWS account, Azure worker plane resource group Key Vault, or GCP project where the orchestrator account is present.

quotes: Create and store the password or key‑pair in AWS Secrets Manager in the AWS account where the orchestrator account is present, and have the ARNs ready for use.
Create and store the secret in the Azure Key Vault of the worker plane resource group in the subscription where the orchestrator account is present, and have the Key Vault URIs ready for use.
Create and store the secret in Secret Manager in the GCP project where the orchestrator account is present, and have the Secret ID paths ready for use.

snowflake-edit-timing.statement: Snowflake account configuration changes take effect only at the next scheduled scan.

quotes: Changes made to the Snowflake account configuration take effect only at the next scheduled scan.

overview-auto-discovery.statement: After a Databricks account is onboarded, DSPM automatically discovers its workspaces and creates the SQL warehouses and access permissions for scans; findings are reported on the Resource Inventory page.

quotes: After a Databricks account is onboarded, DSPM automatically discovers the associated workspaces and creates the necessary SQL warehouses and access permissions to perform scans.
reports the findings on the Resource Inventory page.

workspace-admin.statement: Registering a workspace requires being a workspace admin in the Databricks workspace, who is granted USE CATALOG access to all catalogs.

quotes: You must be a workspace admin in the Databricks workspace.
The workspace admin is granted USE CATALOG access to all catalogs in the workspace.

azure-managed-identity.statement: For Azure workspaces, the orchestrator and scanner managed identities are each added as Microsoft Entra ID managed service principals with the Databricks SQL access and Workspace access entitlements.

quotes: select the Microsoft Entra ID managed option, enter a name for the service principal, and paste the Application ID from the DSPM Databricks registration
- Databricks SQL access
- Workspace access
Repeat these steps for both the orchestrator- and scanner-managed identities.

aws-service-principal.statement: For AWS workspaces, the service principal is added to the admin group so DSPM can calculate entitlements, given Databricks SQL Access and Workspace Access entitlements, and its OAuth secret is stored in the orchestrator account.

quotes: Ensure that the service principal is a member of the admin group to allow DSPM to calculate entitlements.
1. Databricks SQL Access
2. Workspace Access
4. Generate the OAuth secret.
5. Store the secret in the orchestrator account.

connection-string-compute.statement: The JDBC connection string comes from an existing Serverless SQL Warehouse or, if none exists, a new single-node compute with Databricks Runtime 17.1, node type Standard_D2ds_v6 (Azure) or m5d.large (AWS) and termination after 20 minutes of inactivity; the JDBC URL is copied without its last three properties.

quotes: If a Serverless SQL Warehouse exists in the workspace, retrieve its JDBC URL from the SQL Warehouses section.
Single Node: Select the checkbox.
Databricks Runtime: Select 17.1.
- Azure: Select Standard_D2ds_v6.
- AWS: Select m5d.large.
Terminate after X minutes of inactivity: Enter 20.
Copy the URL without the last three properties.

aws-private-link.statement: For AWS customer-managed VPCs, the DSPM orchestrator and scanner subnets must be allowed by network policies or AWS private link.

quotes: For AWS customer-managed VPCs, ensure the DSPM orchestrator and scanner subnets are allowed by network policies or AWS private link.

account-metastore-admin.statement: For an AWS Databricks account, the service principal needs the Account Admin permission and Metastore Admin on the associated workspaces, because a workspace admin does not have access to all catalogs and schemas in the metastore.

quotes: 8. Enable the Account Admin permission.

A Metastore Admin privilege is required as it has access to and manages permissions across all catalogs and schemas, while a workspace admin does not have access to all catalogs and schemas in the metastore.

account-type-aws-only.statement: The Databricks Account registration type is available only for AWS.

quotes: The Account registration type is available only for AWS.

account-discovery-actions.statement: About 15 minutes after a Databricks account is added, DSPM discovers its workspaces, grants the service principal Workspace Admin on each, creates a dedicated 2X-Small SQL warehouse per workspace that auto-terminates after 10 minutes of inactivity, and grants read access to catalogs and schemas.

quotes: within approximately 15 minutes, it performs the following actions:
Grants the service principal Workspace Admin access to each discovered workspace.
Creates a dedicated 2X-Small SQL warehouse in each workspace so that DSPM scans do not interfere with your existing queries.
This dedicated warehouse is configured to auto-terminate after 10 minutes of inactivity.
Grants the service principal read access to the catalogs and schemas.

permission-script-job.statement: For AWS workspaces a Databricks job is recommended to run the permission script because it grants access to newly added catalogs; without a job the script must be re-run for each new catalog.

quotes: create a Databricks job (recommended) or run it manually in the Databricks workspace to grant DSPM the required access.
If a job is not created, you must manually rerun the script every time a new catalog is created in your workspace to ensure DSPM can scan it.

integration-details-azure-only.statement: In the Databricks workspace details drawer, the Integration Details and 'Execute the script in the Databricks Workspace' sections apply only to Azure cloud account configurations; this does not say AWS workspaces have no permission script.

quotes: 3. Integration Details: Applicable only to Azure cloud account configurations.
4. Execute the script in the Databricks Workspace: Applicable only to Azure cloud account configurations.

aws-job-config.statement: The AWS permission-script job is named with the prefix zdspm-job, uses a single-node m5d.large job cluster, runs as the Metastore Admin service principal, and the DSPM service principal is given Can Manage Run.

quotes: Cluster Type: Select Single node.
Create the job using the name prefix zdspm-job.
Node Type: Select m5d.large.
2. Select the service principal provided to DSPM at registration.
3. Grant it permission to Can Manage Run.
Select the created Metastore Admin Service Principal.

ip-access-list.statement: If the IP Access List is enabled in the workspace and has rules that might block access, the scanner and orchestrator egress IPs must be allowlisted at the workspace and also at the account level.

quotes: If the IP Access List is enabled in the workspace and includes rules that might block access to the scanner or orchestrator, allowlist the egress IP addresses where the scanner and orchestrator are hosted.
This configuration is also required at the Account Level.

edit-fields.statement: When editing a Databricks workspace, Client ID and Client Secret ARN are editable for AWS only and Connection String for AWS and Azure; the connection must be verified after updating.

quotes: Client ID (for AWS only): Update the client identifier issued by the cloud provider.
Client Secret ARN (for AWS only): Update the AWS Secrets Manager ARN that stores the client secret.
Connection String (for AWS and Azure): Update the JDBC connection string to connect DSPM to the Databricks workspace.
After updating, you must verify the connection between DSPM and Databricks.

azure-unmanaged-secret-location.summary: For an Azure unmanaged database the Adding Unmanaged Databases table says any Key Vault of the target subscription; prerequisite 6 says the Key Vault of the worker plane resource group in the orchestrator subscription.

positions.says: For an Azure unmanaged database, the secret is created and stored in any Key Vault of the target subscription.

quotes: | Unmanaged | AWS: Create and store the secret in the AWS target account. Azure: Create and store the secret in any Key Vault of the target subscription. |

positions.says: For Azure the secret is stored in the Key Vault of the worker plane resource group in the subscription where the orchestrator account is present; prerequisite 6 gives an unmanaged/on-premises split only for AWS.

quotes: Azure: Create and store the secret in the Azure Key Vault of the worker plane resource group in the subscription where the orchestrator account is present, and have the Key Vault URIs ready for use.

azure-unmanaged-secret-location.impact: Which Key Vault holds an Azure unmanaged database's secret is read two ways on one page; check the console rather than assume either.

snowflake-edit-secret-wording.title: Which secret store the Snowflake edit page means for key-pair secrets
snowflake-edit-secret-wording.detail: Both the edit page and the add page (AWS passphrase, Azure and GCP private key and passphrase) describe key-pair secret fields as a HashiCorp Vault instance ARN/URI or Secret ID path, while the add page for AWS says an AWS Secrets Manager secret; the wording is unclear.

databricks-gcp.title: Whether Databricks on GCP can be registered
databricks-gcp.detail: The Adding Databricks page heads its workspace procedure 'Azure or AWS Workspace' and the Account type is AWS only; no GCP workspace procedure appears and the pages do not say GCP is unsupported.

databricks-script-contents.title: What the Databricks permission script does
databricks-script-contents.detail: The pages say to run the permission script (as a job or manually) but do not show its contents.
